__reason.src/lib/assistant/productHelpRegistry.ts: NOT an extraction target, by its own design. This registry is bilingual at the row level — every topic exists once per locale, and `PRODUCT_HELP_BASE_LOCALE` is `he` because the product is Hebrew-first (OPEN-DECISIONS #192). The Hebrew rows ARE the originals; moving them into the dictionary would delete the base locale the guard compares translations against. What this feature owed here was the missing half: 12 of the 15 topics had no English row, so an English speaker asking the assistant a product question got Hebrew back. All 15 now pair. Counted Hebrew lines therefore stay high and pinned.
__reason.src/lib/exportTemplates.ts: Three lines stay, and all three are the same protected class: `definition.title` is the CANONICAL name of an export template. ExportTemplatesPanel writes it into `p_name` as the default name of the stored template, and composes it into the `p_reason` that lands in audit_logs on both the upload and the approval. What a person READS is `titleKey`, beside it. Everything else on this surface moved: three descriptions, twenty-two field labels and twenty-two samples. The samples are keys too — a sample date reads differently in each language, and a sample business name in a script the reader cannot read illustrates nothing.
__reason.src/lib/format.ts: Every Hebrew line here is a UNIT_FORMS key, and a UNIT_FORMS key is a VALUE STORED IN products.unit — the protected class the plan names: a string that goes INTO the system is not translated. Owner decision #282 keeps that column Hebrew and forbids a data migration; the English word for each unit lives on the canonical row as en: { one, other } and is chosen at render time by formatUnit(), so an English reader sees "3 kg" while the catalogue still holds the Hebrew unit. The spelling variants (a supplier who writes yod-het with an apostrophe, or in the plural) are input recognition in the same class as FieldSpec.aliases in Onboarding.tsx: they are what cleanUnit() matches an uploaded price list against, and replacing them would stop a Hebrew price list from mapping at all. P3-G2 closed on this design, with paired screenshots. Nothing on this surface is copy a person reads from source; the count stays pinned.
